questions.text: A 32-year-old woman falls on an outstretched hand. X-ray confirms a fracture of the radial head. Which nerve is most commonly associated with this injury?

A 30-year-old man presents with a deep laceration over the palm. On examination, sensation over the dorsal aspect of the hand is normal. He is unable to flex the little finger and ring finger. Wasting is found on palmar aspect. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?
options: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve

questions.text: A 30-year-old man requires surgery for a fracture of proximal humerus. The anesthesiologist plans a brachial plexus block that provides anesthesia to the entire upper limb below the shoulder. Following the block, the patient develops ipsilateral facial numbness too. Which block is being performed?

A 48-year-old woman undergoes a minor pelvic surgery involving dissection along the lateral pelvic wall. During the procedure, a nerve that passes through a canal is inadvertently injured. Postoperatively, she has difficulty in adduction of thigh while walking, along with loss of sensation over the medial aspect of the thigh. Which nerve was most likely injured?

A 45-year-old man undergoes a splenectomy following abdominal trauma. During dissection and ligation of the splenic hilum, care must be taken to avoid injury to a vessel. Which of the following vessels is most likely to be injured?

A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a road traffic accident. On examination, he has bilateral periorbital ecchymosis (raccoon eyes) without direct injury to the orbit. Under which layer of the scalp is responsible for it?

Weakness of the contralateral lower half of the face with forehead sparing
Weakness of the contralateral lower half of the face with inability to wrinkle the forehead
Hyperacusis with complete ipsilateral facial weakness

questions.text: A 62-year-old man presents with progressive difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair. After walking for some time, he develops fatigue and falls.
